0 Class of '89 Class of '89 will take you back to the days of big dreams, bigger hair, and the ultimate high school send-off, so break out the neon and dust off your mixtapes — it's time to create the most legendary yearbook spread ever! It's your senior year in high school, and as President of the Yearbook Club, it's your responsibility to make sure every standout moment is captured. Compete to create the most kickin' yearbook by sending your uniquely skilled staff all over the school. Assemble a nerd herd full of brainiacs, a team full of musclehead jocks, or a clique of style mavens who always look funky fresh. From the drama on the football field to the most wack after-school clubs, every righteous memory must be immortalized! Compete to design the gnarliest yearbook spread before the final bell rings. Points can be gained from clever tile placement, strategic set collection, and sweet proximity bonuses as each teacher's class is filled with matching students. Of course, trading signatures will earn much-needed street cred. Don't wig out as only the most awesomely organized yearbooks can win, and nothing is more bodacious than one that is alphabetized. [Rating: 4/10] Simple to play yet unexpectedly thinky puzzler. Place cards and put tokens on them in order to trigger the scoring rules you choose to add to your play area, with some sub games where you race up tracks for bonus paraphernalia and try to land various majority scoring goals.

[Rating: 6/10] Pleasant family weight game with a really cool aesthetic!  Just needed more of a hook or something a little more compelling about the gameplay. Still recommend if you're looking for a light worker placement with a cool theme.

[Rating: 6/10] A cool theme, but a bit too much focus on set collection and the myriad of tokens placed everywhere.

[Rating: 6/10] Make sure you are aware of how everything scores before you play. It helps:). Has some interesting takes on set collection/creation.

[Rating: 7/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  There's a ton of different ways to score and competition over majorities in some of the tags to wrangle over and even a bit of polyomino placement. I had fun playing this on BGA but I am not sure how everyone else playing felt. When this comes out in boardgame form, it is going to be pretty fiddly with little pieces on top of cardboard tiles, moving up tracks, etc.

[Rating: 7/10] One of the American themes of all time. I like the drafting options but there are SO many components.

[Rating: 7.8/10] Played on bga implementation was pretty good.  Lots going on.  Just one play so far looking forward to more plays
